Yes. Two groups of CAPAs share an upstream cause that the recorded root causes don't show. The clearest is CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016. The second is CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015.

**Group 1: the FRZ-80-02 freezer excursion and vector lot LV25-118 (CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016)**

- DEV-26-021 (CAPA-26-008) records the cause as a compressor failure. The FRZ8002 trace shows the freezer climbing from about -80 °C at 01:00 on 20 April to about -36 °C by 15:00. CAPA-26-008 replaced the compressor, and its effectiveness check covers only compressor pull-down. The lot that was in that freezer was not addressed.
- DEV-26-027 (CAPA-26-016) records the cause as donor variability (low CD3 at apheresis). The data don't support that. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 came from donors with normal CD3 (65.3% and 63.8%).
- The shared factor is the vector lot LV25-118. The `material_lot` table records it as stored in FRZ-80-02, which is the freezer in the DEV-26-021 excursion. Every run transduced with LV25-118 after the excursion shows low CAR+ (FC-CAR), while the runs transduced with it before the excursion are normal:
  - Before the excursion (PD26-014 to PD26-023, transduced 5–15 April): FC-CAR 34.5–41.3%.
  - After the excursion: ENG26-01 19.8%, ENG26-02 11.9%, ENG26-03 13.9%, PD26-024 17.3%, PD26-025 14.9%, PD26-026 16.3%, PD26-027 16.0%. These later runs are not all engineering runs. PD26-024 to PD26-027 are platform runs with normal donor CD3.
- Other transduction lots (LV25-104, LV26-007, LV26-021) show no such drop. The donor explanation doesn't hold because donor CD3 was normal in the affected runs.
- CAPA-26-016 targets the wrong cause. DEV-26-027 is still open, and LV25-118 is still listed as RELEASED.

**Group 2: INCubator INC-03 door/latch (CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015)**

- DEV-26-011 (CAPA-26-012) traces to a misaligned INC-03 door switch found during OQ. CAPA-26-012 (replace switch, due 31 March) is still OPEN and overdue, even though the deviation is closed.
- DEV-26-033 (CAPA-26-015) records operator error (latch not confirmed), with PPQ26-02 viability at 75.2% against an 80% criterion. The INC-03 door alarm fired on 10 June, the door was found not fully latched on 11 June, and the alarm was acknowledged at 07:50.
- The shared upstream cause is the unresolved INC-03 door/latch hardware problem. The retraining in CAPA-26-015 addresses the operator step but not the equipment. This is a weaker link than group 1 because it depends on the open hardware CAPA rather than on a shared material.

CAPA-26-019 (supplier sampling-port weld defect on PRDG-01 tubing) has no shared upstream cause with the others.

The most important finding is group 1: the freezer excursion was assessed as low risk, but it appears to have degraded LV25-118 and is affecting CAR+ output in more runs than DEV-26-027 covers.

content.text:
Yes. Two groups of CAPAs share an upstream cause that the recorded root causes don't show. The clearest is CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016. The second is CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015.

**Group 1: the FRZ-80-02 freezer excursion and vector lot LV25-118 (CAPA-26-008 and CAPA-26-016)**

- DEV-26-021 (CAPA-26-008) records the cause as a compressor failure. The FRZ8002 trace shows the freezer climbing from about -80 °C at 01:00 on 20 April to about -36 °C by 15:00. CAPA-26-008 replaced the compressor, and its effectiveness check covers only compressor pull-down. The lot that was in that freezer was not addressed.
- DEV-26-027 (CAPA-26-016) records the cause as donor variability (low CD3 at apheresis). The data don't support that. ENG26-01 and ENG26-02 came from donors with normal CD3 (65.3% and 63.8%).
- The shared factor is the vector lot LV25-118. The `material_lot` table records it as stored in FRZ-80-02, which is the freezer in the DEV-26-021 excursion. Every run transduced with LV25-118 after the excursion shows low CAR+ (FC-CAR), while the runs transduced with it before the excursion are normal:
  - Before the excursion (PD26-014 to PD26-023, transduced 5–15 April): FC-CAR 34.5–41.3%.
  - After the excursion: ENG26-01 19.8%, ENG26-02 11.9%, ENG26-03 13.9%, PD26-024 17.3%, PD26-025 14.9%, PD26-026 16.3%, PD26-027 16.0%. These later runs are not all engineering runs. PD26-024 to PD26-027 are platform runs with normal donor CD3.
- Other transduction lots (LV25-104, LV26-007, LV26-021) show no such drop. The donor explanation doesn't hold because donor CD3 was normal in the affected runs.
- CAPA-26-016 targets the wrong cause. DEV-26-027 is still open, and LV25-118 is still listed as RELEASED.

**Group 2: INCubator INC-03 door/latch (CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015)**

- DEV-26-011 (CAPA-26-012) traces to a misaligned INC-03 door switch found during OQ. CAPA-26-012 (replace switch, due 31 March) is still OPEN and overdue, even though the deviation is closed.
- DEV-26-033 (CAPA-26-015) records operator error (latch not confirmed), with PPQ26-02 viability at 75.2% against an 80% criterion. The INC-03 door alarm fired on 10 June, the door was found not fully latched on 11 June, and the alarm was acknowledged at 07:50.
- The shared upstream cause is the unresolved INC-03 door/latch hardware problem. The retraining in CAPA-26-015 addresses the operator step but not the equipment. This is a weaker link than group 1 because it depends on the open hardware CAPA rather than on a shared material.

CAPA-26-019 (supplier sampling-port weld defect on PRDG-01 tubing) has no shared upstream cause with the others.

The most important finding is group 1: the freezer excursion was assessed as low risk, but it appears to have degraded LV25-118 and is affecting CAR+ output in more runs than DEV-26-027 covers.
